# RSNA Knee Abnormality Detection — Discoveries

This file holds **what is known**: every claim, its numbers and interpretation, and its verification state. Every agent reads all of it. `handoff.md` only points here by ID.

Verification is per **host**, not per agent: a discovery made on one host (for example Codex) is cross-checked **once** by a different host (for example Claude Code). Sessions on the same host do not re-review each other.

Discovery IDs use `D-<Agent>-<NNN>`, numbered by the agent that creates the discovery, for example `D-A-001` or `D-B-014`.

> Read the **Index** first (one line per discovery, generated 2026-10-15 from 292 entries); open a full entry when it matters. New discoveries are appended to the end of the file AND get one index row (B adds the row in the same edit).

### Most decision-relevant findings

1. **Current recorded best:** H189 public **0.958** (D-B-213); H190 ties .958 and H195 is .957 (D-B-217). Preserve exact scored versions; private transfer remains unmeasured.
2. **Public gains that transferred:** own AUG1 R50 **0.931 vs 0.925** (+0.006); historical B3-AUG1 **0.950**; A5q **0.954 vs A5 0.952** (D-B-080, D-B-137).
3. **More blending did not establish a gain:** vNext-A/B **0.955 = C85**; vNext-R7-A **0.956 < C85-R7 0.957**; multi-change tests do not isolate own-weight causality (D-B-167, D-B-179).
4. **OAI benefit failed locally:** EXP155 and OAI-free EXP143v2 both public **0.946**; corrected-OAI cold fit macro **-0.0078** with negative CI (D-B-101, D-B-139).
5. **L2 supervision replicated across families:** 75% Dread/25% aquila yields five-fold JEV gains **+0.0050 R50, +0.0054 ConvNeXt-T, +0.0058 DINO-base** (D-B-095, D-B-098, D-B-111).
6. **Best aligned partner evidence:** adding Small to deployed Q7 gains five-fold macro **+0.0011 [+.0008,+.0014]**, weak4 **+0.0012**, every fold positive; OOF evidence (D-B-157).
7. **Strong-teacher PL failed its gate:** EXPOSED R7 global50/50 macro **+0.0030** but weak4 **-0.0002** and slightly negative image-read lenses; silent fill harmful; **NO_GO** (D-B-180).
8. **Higher resolution failed its gate:** native320 fold1 macro **+0.0029 [+.0007,+.0054]**, yet a seed/target cell below **-0.005** fails the registered floor; **NO_GO** (D-B-184).
9. **Release engineering failures are distinct:** v1.2.2 loses own predictions to worker pickling; eight rebases hang; strict v1.1.0 byte patch completes visible run in about **11 min** (D-B-182, D-B-183).
10. **Validation limits remain binding:** ordinary five-fold OOF cannot validate nested fitted stackers; Gold58 is exposed; no untouched ancestry-eligible fluid panel exists (D-B-160, D-A-002, D-B-171).

---

Use this exact format:

```markdown
## D-B-001 — Short title
- Source: B
- Host: Codex
- User: <user name>
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Cross-check: VERIFIED
- Finding: ...
- Evidence: ...
- Implication: ...
- Reviews:
  - Claude Code (A): CLOSED — reproduced independently with ...
```

`Cross-check` states:

- `PENDING`: no different host has reviewed it yet. New discoveries start here, with an empty `Reviews:` list.
- `REVIEWING <Host> (<Agent>)`: a different-host session has claimed the review.
- `VERIFIED`: a different host reviewed it and recorded `CLOSED`.
- `HOLD`: a different host needs specific evidence, a condition change, or an improvement first.
- `CHALLENGED`: a host found a material contradiction, flaw, or missing assumption.

Rules:

- The source does not review its own discovery.
- Review only discoveries whose `Host` differs from yours and whose `Cross-check` is `PENDING` (or `HOLD` when its condition is now met). Claim it first with `REVIEWING <your host> (<your agent>)`.
- One cross-host review is enough; add another only for high-impact or disputed discoveries.
- Review lines use `<Host> (<Agent>): CLOSED | HOLD | CHALLENGED — reason`. `HOLD` and `CHALLENGED` must say what would make the discovery acceptable.
- When the source revises a `HOLD` or `CHALLENGED` discovery, it updates `Evidence`, keeps the old reviews, and resets `Cross-check` to `PENDING`.
- If only one host is available, a different slot on the same host may cross-check; begin its reason with `same host —`.
- Use `VERIFIED` discoveries freely. A plan item built on a `PENDING`, `REVIEWING`, or `HOLD` discovery must say so in its `Evidence`. Do not build on `CHALLENGED` discoveries until resolved.

Every completed experiment or test creates or updates exactly one discovery here, whatever the outcome, so this file is the only index of what has been tried:

- positive: `Finding: <claim>`
- negative: `Finding: <claim> does not hold under <conditions>`
- inconclusive: `Finding: inconclusive — <what was tried and why it did not settle>`

A cross-check updates the reviewed discovery instead of creating a new one. Before adding a plan item, every agent searches this file first.

When a result beats the project's current best, start its `Implication` with `new current best:` and update `Current best` in `handoff.md` Shared state in the same step, citing this discovery.

A discovery may generate many plan hypotheses, and one hypothesis may combine many discoveries. When moving an idea back into `plan.md`, always include the source IDs plus the concrete `Evidence` and `Improvement` that justify the new attempt.

Do not archive this file merely because it grows; merge duplicate discoveries instead.

D-A-017 onward are one discovery per completed experiment or test from the legacy records (chronological). Legacy originals: `docs/legacy/discoveries.md`, `docs/research/`, `docs/handoffs/`. ## D-B-002 — Per-scanner / field-strength score offsets do not explain pooled AUC loss: cross-fitted group offsets lower macro for B and R384
- Source: B
- Host: Claude Code
- User: kim
- Date: 2026-10-06
- Cross-check: VERIFIED
- Finding: A per-group, per-finding additive logit offset (5-fold component-grouped cross-fit inside V888) does not hold as an improvement mechanism: for B the macro change is field −0.0021 / scanner_group −0.0047 / manufacturer −0.0054 / cached_mask −0.0005 (label-free centering) and −0.0012 / −0.0032 / −0.0032 / +0.0013 (label-aware); for R384 −0.0019 / −0.0050 / −0.0047 / −0.0007 and −0.0021 / −0.0048 / −0.0028 / +0.0015. Only the cached-mask label-aware variant is marginally positive (+0.0013/+0.0015), an in-sample-label diagnostic, not a usable method. (updated 2026-10-07 16:48 KST) Scope correction. This tests two specific mean-centering estimators, cross-fitted on 5 component folds of V888 with weak Dread labels: label-free group centering, which also removes real between-group prevalence differences; a label-aware class-mean offset, which falls back to a single class in 6–8% of field/scanner/manufacturer offsets and 1% of cached-mask offsets. "In-sample" means "fitted on other V888 folds", not on the same rows. It is not an upper bound, because no optimal per-group intercept was searched.
- Evidence: `artifacts/experiments/EXP092_GROUP_OFFSET_DIAG/result.json` (tool `tools/exp092_group_offset_diag.py`, CPU only); groups from `EXP084_GROUP_R34_LOSS_PROTOCOL/group-metadata.csv`; Dread labels np.rint; seed 20261003 fold assignment.
- Implication: the group differences seen in D-A-042/D-A-039 are not a simple calibration/intercept shift that re-centering can recover; metadata-conditioned calibration is closed as a cheap lever. Domain differences, if any, sit in ranking within groups. (updated 2026-10-07 16:48 KST) Replaces "metadata-conditioned calibration is closed as a cheap lever" and "domain differences sit in ranking within groups". These two estimators did not help on reused V888 predictions. Other calibration forms, and the cause of the group AUC differences, are untested.
- Reviews:
  - Codex (C): CHALLENGED — 2026-10-07 13:46 KST, All 16 reported macro deltas reproduce exactly from saved V888 predictions and Dread float32-rounded labels. B baseline 0.8933965283111673; R384 baseline 0.8953547410264552. Cached-mask label-aware deltas are +0.0013319393486085351/+0.001456391287537162; every other tested variant is negative. The negative mean-centering experiment does not identify the causal source of pooled AUC loss or close all metadata-conditioned calibration. Label-free group centering can remove real prevalence signal; label-aware centering estimates means rather than an optimal intercept and sometimes uses only one class when the other has fewer than five cases. The offset prediction for each row is cross-fitted, so calling it row-level in-sample would also be inaccurate. Development reuse/selected checkpoints remain separate limitations. Acceptance requires: Retain this as a negative result for the specified mean-centering estimators on reused V888 weak-label predictions. Replace claims that simple calibration is disproved or all remaining domain differences must be within-group ranking. No new experiment is needed to make that bounded finding acceptable. Evidence: `.local/crosscheck-20261007-1333/implementation/reproduced.json` and `implementation/verdicts.json` in the same audit directory (exact path/line bindings and per-claim limits).
  - Codex (C): CLOSED — 2026-10-07 17:42 KST, The16:48 narrowing resolves the prior challenge. Retained independently reproduced16 deltas remain a result for these two cross-fitted mean-centering estimators on reused weak V888, not an optimal-intercept bound or causal account of domain loss. The small cached-mask positives remain exploratory. It does not rule out all metadata calibration, and no new calibration search is justified by merely correcting this scope. Evidence: `.local/crosscheck-20261007-1333/implementation/reproduced.json`, `implementation/verdicts.json`, `metrics/reproduction.json`; `.local/crosscheck-amendments-20261007-1730/remaining-verdicts.json`.

- Source: B

Removing V888 rows from the fit does not remove that dependence; the tool's caveat "V888 used only for evaluation" (`tools/exp093_cross_target_stacker.py:91`) is wrong at pipeline level.

## D-B-005 — Anchor 0.943 runtime structure: eight sequential phases, every phase decodes DICOM itself, CoAt families run one at a time for N>48; realistic low-risk saving is ~0.3–0.5 h at 1,300 studies, not 1–2 h
- Source: B
- Host: Claude Code
- User: kim
- Date: 2026-10-06
- Cross-check: VERIFIED
- Finding: Static read of the anchor source (`docs/handoffs/evidence/2026-10/2026-10-03-anchor-study/anchor_source.py`, cell markers match the notebook) and the instrumented D01 child: phases run strictly one after another (DINOv2 → A5 → RadImageNet → Raptor → CoAt ×4 → stacker/rank); no DataParallel; CoAt families are subprocesses with one worker per T4 and switch to fully sequential families when N>48 (L4483–4497, env RSNA_PARALLEL_COAT_READERS; stated reason: host RAM/contention). Every phase decodes DICOM with its own recipe (DINO 336/12 slices/130 mm; A5 336/16; Rad 3×224/8; Raptor 140 mm up to 96 slices with 3 preparations; CoAt 384/130 mm with family-specific grids), so no decoded tensor can be shared across families without changing outputs; only raw pixel arrays/header order could. Per 100 studies both GPUs idle for ~57 s (DINO cache decode), ~26 s (DINO model load), ~48 s (Rad first layout), ~26–33 s × 4 (CoAt parent overhead); one GPU idles ~66 s in CoAt shard tails; D4 appears CPU-prep bound. Host RAM, not VRAM (1.9–2.5 GB/shard), limits concurrency: cgroup current reached 24.3 GiB at 100 studies including page cache (parent RSS 8 GiB); a parallel CoAt pair adds ~6–10 GiB. A failed CoAt child is non-fatal and silently re-weights the remaining arms (L4558). The anchor is probably not bit-reproducible (GPU batches pair studies in prep-completion order), so "identical outputs" must be judged within the existing 0.002 tolerance after comparing two unmodified runs. (updated 2026-10-07 16:48 KST) Corrections: (a) 24,265,555,968 bytes is 22.60 GiB (24.27 GB). It is the largest end-of-phase cgroup snapshot, including reclaimable page cache, not a measured peak (anchor100-review.json memory.notes). (b) A failed or rejected CoAt child is logged, not silent: anchor_source.py prints "FAILED; continuing without it (flagged)" at :4352/:4411/:4433/:4478 and emits `rsna_event coat_*_output_rejected` at :4518–:4557. The remaining members are re-weighted and the run continues. (c) The 0.002 tolerance for anchor outputs is superseded by D-B-018. Two unmodified 100-study runs differ in 520/1,200 final cells (max 0.10, mean 0.0062), so comparisons of a modified anchor use the unmodified-repeat spread.
- Evidence: explore-agent report 2026-10-06 (line references above); `docs/handoffs/evidence/2026-10/2026-10-03-anchor-runtime-cost/anchor100-review.json` (phase timings per 100 studies: dinov2 276 s, a5 88, rad 92, raptor 410, residual_coat 336, global96 340, d4 197, repairv1 260; total 2,031 s). Ranked options: (1) each CoAt family on one whole GPU, two families at a time (~900 s at 1,300; low–medium risk; needs the device_count()==2 asserts bypassed); (2) overlap D4 with a GPU-bound family (≤1,300 s, medium, CPU contention on ~4 vCPU); (3) pre-decode A5/Rad in a separate process during DINO/Raptor GPU work (500–1,000 s, medium; in-process is unsafe because A5/Rad rewrite globals); (4) load DINO members during cache decode (~25 s); (5) rebalance Raptor arms after per-worker timing; (6) one decode shared by the four CoAt families (largest CPU cut, high risk, prep-code identity across artifacts unverified).
- Implication: H-B-14 alone cannot create the budget for anchor + own E1 (anchor 26,400 s + B224 8,500 s + R384 ~2,500–3,500 s ≈ 10.4–10.7 h at 1,300); the larger lever is to run the own arms on the anchor's already-prepared Raptor inputs (same 140 mm/336 px contract as our corpus, D-A-017) so their cost drops from decode-dominated ~6.5 s/study to model compute only — to be verified against our serving outputs on the 100 engineering studies. Any anchor modification must add a hard assertion that all four CoAt children succeeded. (updated 2026-10-07 16:48 KST) The 10.4–10.7 h budget and the 0.3–0.5 h savings are estimates made before D-B-018. They are superseded by the 7.6–7.95 h projection with shared decode. Saved 100-study anchor elapsed is 2031.042859639 s; linear 1300 projection 26403.557175307 s. Runtime savings remain estimates, not measured optimized-full-run bounds. ## D-B-016 — Public LB as a measuring instrument: on ≈390 public studies, the difference between two separately trained models moves by about ±0.007–0.010 (95%) from sampling alone
- Source: B
- Host: Claude Code
- User: kim
- Date: 2026-10-07
- Cross-check: VERIFIED
- Finding: Resampling ≈390-study subsets (public ≈30% of ≈1,300) of the G1 V888 predictions by whole components (400 draws, without replacement, Dread labels rounded): SD of the macro-12 difference was 0.0014 for the same weights with an inference change (B K36 − B), 0.0028–0.0032 for two separately trained runs (BF16 control − B; student − control), and 0.0037 for two different models (R384 − B). After the finite-population correction for drawing 390 of 888 (÷0.75) this is ≈0.0019, ≈0.0037–0.0043 and ≈0.0049, i.e. 95% ranges of about ±0.004 for inference-only changes and ±0.007–0.010 between separately trained models. Single-run arms add trajectory (seed) noise on top (0.006–0.011 between runs so far, D-B-009/D-B-010; the clean local value comes from H-B-17). Choosing the better of two arms by public score inflates the winner by about half an SD (≈0.002). (updated 2026-10-07 16:48 KST) Scope: these are resampling SDs of fixed G1 V888 predictions scored against rounded Dread labels (weak, report-derived). They are a proxy for how much a 390-study subset can move a difference, not a measurement or a CI of the real public difference, which uses official image-read labels and an unknown public prevalence. The ÷0.75 finite-population factor is a heuristic for a clustered AUC. "Trajectory noise 0.006–0.011" should read: one same-machine seed difference of −0.0060 (D-B-017); −0.0064 and −0.011 were confounded T4 runs. The ≈0.002 winner inflation is the formula E|d|/2 ≈ 0.4·SD(d) under equal true scores, not a measurement. How the private split tracks public is unmeasured.
- Evidence: scratchpad public_noise.py (2026-10-07) on EXP084_B_G1, EXP090_COV_BF16_CTRL, EXP095_STUDENT_B8, EXP096 R384 K24 and B K36 predictions; the private split is ≈910 studies and only partly tracks public differences.
- Implication: public LB overfits easily if used for tuning, so (1) no ratio, weight, threshold or recipe tuning on public (D-A-010 stands); (2) at most a few pre-registered binary decisions with large expected effects, comparing 5-fold ensembles rather than single runs; (3) label interventions, which only official labels can score, are decided by the prior evidence (D-A-022, D-B-013, D-B-014) plus a pre-registered public guard against a clear loss, not by demanding a public gain; (4) non-label changes (architecture, inference, ensembling) are decided by 5-fold OOF on all 4,343 studies (11× the public size); (5) of the two final selections, one is the robust choice backed by CV and priors and the other the best public score if it differs. (updated 2026-10-07 16:48 KST) Points (1)–(5) stand as operational policy. The pre-registered public thresholds (+0.009 / −0.005, 0.920 / 0.914, −0.005) are decision rules sized against this proxy, not significance tests.
- Reviews:
  - Codex (A): CHALLENGED — reviewer astra — read-only rerun of preserved public_noise.py reproduces subset SD 0.0028/0.0032/0.0037/0.0014. These are conditional resamples of fixed G1 predictions against rounded Dread labels, not official Public outcomes. Division by 0.75 does not establish a Public macro-AUC CI or noninferiority margin; exchangeability and unequal component-size effects are unverified. Accept after title/implication are narrowed to weak-label resampling sensitivity and FPC heuristic, with private tracking/winner-inflation claims explicitly unmeasured. Keep historical preregistered thresholds as operational rules. Script path and evidence in .local/crosscheck-20261007-1130/astra-review.json.
  - Codex (C): CLOSED — 2026-10-07 17:33 KST, The16:48 amendment resolves the earlier challenge for conditional weak-label subset sensitivity only. Retained independent script review reproduced the four SDs; no bootstrap repeated. The FPC is heuristic, winner inflation is a stated equal-true-score formula rather than measured selection bias, and actual Public/private sampling uncertainty is unknown. The old title and public-CI/private-tracking wording are superseded by the explicit scope correction. Operational thresholds are not significance/noninferiority margins; this CLOSED does not certify their numerical calibration or a private-score guarantee. Downstream plans must retain that limitation. Evidence: `.local/crosscheck-amendments-20261007-1730/evidence.json`, retained independent receipts cited there and `.local/crosscheck-20261007-1130/astra-review.json`.

- Source: C

The frozen converter maps na to 0.05 except Synovitis na to clipped 0.6 x raw Effusion p; the latter rule therefore supplies most Synovitis training targets. These are prior/proxy assumptions, not newly observed image truth or an independently calibrated probability. The competition host directly confirms that official labels were assigned independently from images, image labels are authoritative on disagreement, an official negative means annotated absent, and report-image discrepancies are expected because the reporting workflow differs from multiple readers using stricter thresholds.
- Evidence: .local/strategy-assessment-20261007/audit_label_states.py and audit.json (per-target state/value inventory and source hashes); tools/exp109_relabel_v1.py:43; docs/runbooks/relabel-prompt-v1_1.md; raw .local/relabel/out/b00..b24.jsonl and storage/labels/derived_relabel/provenance.json. Primary host answer: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rsna-knee-abnormality-detection/discussion/733826, fetched with kaggle skill topic --max-chars 5000 on 2026-10-07 13:28 KST. Existing Gold extraction diagnostic was read from artifacts/experiments/EXP109_RELABEL_V1_GOLD_DIAG/diag.json, not rerun; its session result remains in B's 13:22 handoff event. No report text was exported and no model, label file, prompt, running job or submission was changed.
- Implication: Prioritising supervision is a reasonable hypothesis because training-label changes can help without increasing deployment model count, but neither a 0.947-0.948 ceiling nor label improvement being necessary/sufficient for 0.95 follows from current experiments. D-A-042/D-B-023/D-B-026/D-B-028 reject or limit tested configurations, not all resolution/input/training strategies; D-B-018 already shows that shared decoding can fit a bounded extra ensemble in a projected budget. Report extraction errors, report-image information gaps, and arbitrary missingness conversions need different remedies. A stronger LLM cannot recover an unreported image finding with certainty; disagreement and positive-rate shifts measure intervention size rather than correctness, and LLM p is not automatically calibrated. AUC rewards ordering, so stricter binary decisions alone are not evidence of improvement. Use blinded, evidence-span-supported report audits to establish extraction/definition fidelity; preserve explicit negative, below-threshold, uncertain and unmentioned states. Missingness masking, uncertainty weights or image-teacher support remain hypotheses requiring their own controlled tests. For model comparisons use the same held-out IDs and fixed evaluation reference(s), exclude relevant model/teacher ancestors, and do not compare old-model/old-label AUC with new-model/new-label AUC as an improvement. Existing H-A-06, H-B-26 and H-B-28 cover these decisions; no duplicate task or Gold-based tuning is justified. The existing Gold diagnostic and report-label AUC do not establish a ceiling on image-model performance.

## D-C-019 — Inference data pruning: preserve normalization dependencies; shared decode is established, smaller input needs a new accuracy comparison
- Source: C
- Host: Codex
- User: Taeyang
- Date: 2026-10-07
- Cross-check: VERIFIED
- Finding: (recorded 2026-10-07 21:24 KST) Current training/src/raptor_dicom.py:294-318 selects series and decodes only unique sampled slice indices, then computes p2/p98 from all selected slices with repeated samples retaining their multiplicity. Thus a slice absent from a particular CNN window may still affect normalization and is not proven unused. Lines328-334 already perform a physical crop and resize to fixed img x img: a tighter physical crop with unchanged output size does not reduce the encoder tensor shape or its nominal compute; compressed-image decoding can also still require the full frame. Reducing disk bytes or removing background is therefore not, by itself, evidence of lower end-to-end inference time.
- Evidence: static source training/src/raptor_dicom.py:276-334, no data modified or inference run. D-B-018 VERIFIED supplies the prior100-study shared-decode/input-parity and own-prediction-parity evidence, with full-hidden-runtime still projected. D-B-012 VERIFIED supplies the prior fixed-checkpoint K12 loss versus K24 on weak G1 validation (about0.009-0.015), so indiscriminate window removal is not an untested free optimization. D-B-032's numerical62-window cost/gain and non-adoption decision were reproduced, while its stronger interpretation remains CHALLENGED; do not repeat that experiment or treat its failed operational gate as proof of zero benefit.
- Implication: For a hypothetical1300-study submission,32400/1300=24.923seconds per study is an end-to-end wall-time average on the complete allocated machine, including startup/loading/output overhead; it is not a per-GPU allowance or verified hidden test size. An8-hour engineering target leaves one hour of margin and averages22.154seconds/study. Saving5seconds/study would save6500seconds(1.806h), an arithmetic scenario rather than a measured new speedup. Prioritize avoiding duplicate header/pixel decoding and sharing exactly compatible preprocessing across models; share raw pixels and render separately when model contracts differ. Measure stage wall times, peak memory and long-study tails, since overlapping stages prevent summing component savings. Fewer windows/series, adaptive anatomical selection or smaller tensor resolution can save compute but change the prediction recipe; compare fixed checkpoints on identical study/split/labels/mask/targets, especially rare findings, before adoption. Keep every required study/target scored and preserve original datasets. Existing B29 covers common preparation for label ensembles and B41 covers headers/prefetch; D-B-018 is completed work to reuse, not a new experiment. No new pruning training, GPU job or duplicate plan admitted from this explanation alone.
